messages:
mike: heads-up — CI microbench for PR #8347 just crossed the perf threshold on our batch-fanout test :grimacing:

rachel: ugh, link? what metric spiked?

mike: https://github.com/redwood-inference/repo/pull/8347
mike: the failing test is `microbench/batcher/fanout_latency` — baseline 95p = 42ms, this run = 57ms (threshold 50ms)

ci-bot: CI artifact uploaded: https://ci.redwood.internal/artifacts/8347/fanout-bench/2187654321, raw numbers and flamegraphs included

rachel: can you paste the summary numbers?

mike: summary from artifact:
```
baseline: p50=12ms p95=42ms p99=76ms
pr8347:   p50=13ms p95=57ms p99=102ms
delta: +1ms p50, +15ms p95, +26ms p99 (~35% at p95)
```

mike: also saw KV cache hit drop from 0.82 -> 0.69 on the synthetic workload, and average batch wait increased 1.2ms -> 3.8ms

yusuf: hmm, PR description mentioned "kernel selector refactor + fanout routing fix" — could be kernel heuristics now choosing a higher-cost kernel for short sequences

yusuf: two obvious next steps: 1) bisect the PR commits locally against microbench harness 2) re-run with `KERNEL_SELECTOR=legacy` env to force old decision

lina: can we hold the rollout? this is in the post-merge train right? If it's blocking the perf gating we should revert until root cause identified :point_up:

mike: it's still in PR stage but merged into the integration branch yesterday. CI for the branch failed the golden perf gate, so rollback may be required for the merge window

rachel: mike, try yusuf's env override first and post the comparison. if that pins it, we have a clear suspect

mike: doing that now. running `./bench/local_run.sh --target fanout --env KERNEL_SELECTOR=legacy`

(10m)

mike: results with legacy selector:
```
legacy: p50=12ms p95=44ms p99=79ms
vs pr8347: p95 drops from 57 -> 44 (back within threshold)
KV hit stays ~0.80
batch wait ~1.3ms
```

mike: so selector refactor looks like the culprit — it's picking a different kernel that increases latency for short sequences and reduces KV reuse

yusuf: confirmed. the new heuristic favors throughput-optimized kernels when estimated batch sizes exceed X, but our fanout synthetic skews batch shape. we need to add a short-seq safety check or bias by active kv-hitrate

lina: proposed immediate action: revert the selector change in the integration branch, open follow-up to adjust heuristics and add a microbench covering fanout distribution. any objections?

rachel: +1 revert for stability. add the microbench as a mandatory golden for that selector area

mike: I'll open the revert PR and mark it as rollout-blocker. also adding a reproducer and the perf flamegraphs to the ticket: https://go.redwood/ticket/RT-4122

ci-bot: Revert PR created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/repo/pull/8351 (labels: rollback, perf-blocker)

yusuf: after revert, we should also add a unit test for kernel selection that simulates skewed batch shapes and asserts no >10% p95 regression against legacy

lina: agreed. let's also track KV cache hit metric in the perf dashboard for that selector change so future regressions alert earlier

mike: thanks — I'll coordinate the revert + follow-up. ping me if you want to help with the microbench or the selector patch. :thumbsup:

rachel: awesome, thanks for quick bisect and repro. keep the thread updated once revert lands

mike: will do.
